title: Yeshe Tsogyal
hook: honored as Padmasambhava's closest student and a great teacher herself

segments.voice: Yesterday: Machig Labdrön and chöd, cutting the grip of self. Your line: offer it to fear.

A small yellow scroll, rolled tight, pressed into a crack in a cliff and sealed over with stone. Nobody is meant to find it this year, or the next. In Tibetan tradition, some teachings were hidden like this on purpose, the stories say, waiting for the right person at the right time. And the one who wrote many of them down and helped hide them, the stories say, was a woman. She is honored as Padmasambhava's student and companion, and as a teacher in her own right. Today, Yeshe Tsogyal.
screen: `A SCROLL IN A CLIFF.` → `HIDDEN ON PURPOSE.` → `A WOMAN WROTE THEM DOWN.`

segments.voice: First, who she is in the story. Tibetan tradition remembers her as a young noblewoman who wanted a life of practice more than the marriage planned for her. In time she became the student, and the consort, of Padmasambhava, the teacher from India whom Tibetans call Guru Rinpoche. Second, the keeper of the words. Tradition says she held his teachings in memory, wrote them in a coded script, and hid them as terma, treasures, so that later teachers, called treasure finders, could reveal them when people were ready. In this way of seeing, a teaching can wait for its listener. Third, a teacher herself. Her life story tells of long retreats in caves and snow, of hardship, of healing the sick, and of students of her own, who kept learning from her after Padmasambhava left Tibet. She is not only the one who listened; she is also the one who taught. Fourth, the great mother. In the Nyingma school, Yeshe Tsogyal is honored as wisdom itself in a woman's form. Her devotees connect her with the Perfection of Wisdom, which Buddhist texts call the mother of all Buddhas, and so with the great mother. That title is not about having children. It is about wisdom as the source from which awakening is born. Different Tibetan schools hold her in different degrees of devotion, and these stories come chiefly from the Nyingma tradition.
screen: `A NOBLEWOMAN WHO CHOSE PRACTICE.` · `SHE HID THE TEACHINGS AS TREASURE.` · `A TEACHER WITH STUDENTS OF HER OWN.` · `WISDOM IN A WOMAN'S FORM.` · then, large: `THE GREAT MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one woman who taught you something that stayed: a grandmother, a schoolteacher, a coach, a coworker, a friend. Remember one thing she taught you, in words or just by how she lived, and on each out-breath send her your thanks, wherever she is now.
Yeshe Tsogyal. Padmasambhava's student, keeper of his hidden teachings, a teacher herself, honored in the Nyingma school as the great mother of wisdom. Today's word.
Your line: the great mother. A teaching can wait for its listener. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the Nyingma school, Yeshe Tsogyal is honored in prayers and visualizations alongside Padmasambhava, her life story is read and taught, and Nyingma practitioners receive teachings from treasure texts that tradition says she helped conceal.
